title: Freeze one resource typestate dataflow slice
conditions: Production implementation may not start until states, transitions, joins, diagnostics, invalidation, and bounded-memory evidence are frozen.
goal: Select and freeze the smallest canonical resource typestate/dataflow closure that OPT-G can safely consume.
description: Scope: the complete OPT-F design and acceptance artifacts for one independently executable resource scenario. Context: resource state is currently distributed across Sema binding facts, topology validation, lowering, codegen cleanup, and runtime error settlement. Target: select one active-syntax resource family and freeze a single authoritative state model, transfer functions, joins, convergence, diagnostics, invalidation, and measurable memory bound. Design Considerations: compare mature ownership and monotone dataflow analyses, dense versus sparse facts, worklists, dominance, and cache invalidation against the local pattern catalog. Design Value: removes duplicated state inference without introducing another verifier or parallel resource type system. Constraints & Risks: preserve current syntax and diagnostics, keep failures/effects separate from typestate, complete any migrated state ownership with no compatibility path, and leave unrelated resource families and OPT-G stream scheduling out of scope.

decisions.composition: one canonical resource state owner and one bounded scenario
decisions.algorithms: to be frozen after monotone dataflow and ownership-analysis comparison
decisions.data_structures: state lattice, sparse facts, dependency-indexed worklist, or simpler proven equivalent
decisions.state: uninitialized, open, eof, closed, and materialized are candidate facts; runtime failures remain effects
decisions.isolation: design and executable acceptance artifacts only
decisions.concurrency: OPT-F follows OPT-E and must close before OPT-G activation

test_seams: typestate transition and bounded-work benchmark probe

acceptance_criteria.text: Architecture and Validation freeze one active resource scenario, one state owner, state transitions and joins, deterministic diagnostics, invalidation, convergence, and bounded-memory evidence.
The pattern assessment compares the simplest direct solution with applicable mature dataflow and ownership designs and records an executable proof.

title: Implement conditional file-handle typestate joins
goal: Make CondFlow resource consumption a deterministic may-closed union while preserving current file-handle diagnostics and effects.
description: Closure: module - conditional file-handle typestate join. Context: CondFlow snapshots local binding facts but not consumed-resource facts, so branch state leaks and post-join state is not derived. Target: implement branch-isolated snapshots and a union join over the existing SymbolId-authoritative consumed-resource facts, expose bounded counters, and make this the sole conditional resource-state path. Design Considerations: structured forward flow, O(1) transfers, O(C*R) joins, missing-else identity, invalid-SymbolId fallback, and effects kept separate. Design Value: closes one path-sensitivity gap without a CFG or second typestate system. Constraints & Risks: preserve syntax and diagnostics, no compatibility behavior, and do not enter OPT-G.

interfaces.name: conditional resource typestate
interfaces.inputs: incoming consumed-resource facts and reachable branch ASTs
interfaces.outputs: SymbolId-authoritative may-closed union and bounded counters

decisions.composition: one structured CondFlow transfer and union join
decisions.algorithms: single forward branch evaluation with set union
decisions.data_structures: existing string/SymbolId consumed-resource hash sets plus scalar counters
decisions.state: open is absence and may-closed is presence; failure effects are separate
decisions.concurrency: request-local Sema state; OPT-G waits for completion

acceptance_criteria.text: Conditional file-handle state uses one branch-isolated may-closed union with stable SymbolId authority, diagnostics, missing-else behavior, and reopen transfer.
The old implicit branch-state leak is removed, effects remain separate, and no CFG, second state map, verifier, or compatibility path exists.
Focused positive, negative, security, and 256-join counter evidence meets the frozen time and storage budgets.

title: Validate conditional resource typestate dataflow
conditions: Immediate decision issues must be resolved; deferred decisions remain collected for the final OPT-D-G handoff.
goal: Review OPT-F once and run its complete impacted resource-state, security, benchmark, and documentation regression.
description: Scope: the complete conditional file-handle typestate group. Context: group completion requires one fresh end-to-end review followed by one impacted regression. Target: prove branch isolation, conservative union, stable diagnostics, reopen behavior, bounded state work, and complete removal of implicit branch leakage. Design Considerations: inspect changed Sema paths and direct acceptance fixtures only. Design Value: closes OPT-F as a canonical fact boundary ready for OPT-G. Constraints & Risks: one Reviewer only; no general CFG or repeated full regression without failure evidence.

decisions.composition: one group review then one impacted regression
decisions.isolation: OPT-F changed paths and impacted resource tests

acceptance_criteria.text: No unresolved immediate decision issue remains and the Reviewer confirms the frozen OPT-F boundary.
All impacted typestate, resource-topology, security, benchmark, diff, and documentation gates pass once.
